description: The Supreme Court considered Igbo customary law prohibiting females from inheriting from a father who died intestate, and held the custom unconstitutional as violating section 42. Regardless of the circumstances of a female child's birth, she is entitled to inherit; the contrary custom is void.
energy_note: Settled, at the highest court, in 2014.

description: A study across five South-Eastern states found most respondents were unaware of the judgment and compliance was very low. Traditional practice still excludes many women from land and property, leaving widows destitute.
money_note: Value of the share not received.
energy_note: A constitutional right that the village has not heard of.

description: Enforcing the right means suing brothers and uncles, in a court in a town, with a lawyer, over years - at the cost of the family relationships that are the only safety net she has.
energy_note: Winning the land, and losing everyone.

aspect: Which is why most do not
description: The rational calculation for a woman with no independent income is to accept the customary outcome rather than spend years and money to obtain a judgment the family will ignore anyway.
energy_note: A right that costs more than it is worth to claim.

description: Her father died in 2019 without a will. There are four children; she is the only daughter. Her brothers have divided it three ways and are pleasant to her about it. A lawyer in Awka says she would probably win in about four years. She has decided not to, and has not told anyone why.
energy_note: Entitled, informed, and choosing the family instead.
